My land is 4.1 mu, same plot for both crops since I rotate wheat and maize every year — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. I've done this my whole life. My mother farmed this way, my grandmother farmed this way. That's how we do it in Quzhou.

**Wheat:** I'll sow around October 5th, just after National Day holiday when the soil temperature is right. I buy improved variety seeds from the village cooperative — same kind the neighbors use, Jimai or Kenong type, whatever they have. I put down compound fertilizer before sowing with the rotary tiller pass, then topdress urea at jointing in April. For water: I always do the winter irrigation in late November or December to protect the roots, jointing water in late March, and heading water in May. Three times. Last year the spring was dry so I might do a fourth. For pests, I spray herbicide in early spring and then check for powdery mildew and aphids before heading — two sprays usually handles it.

**Maize:** The day the wheat combine finishes, I'm already planning to plant maize — can't waste a single day in summer. I use hybrid seeds, everyone does now, the yields are just better. Rotary till the stubble under first, then plant. Compound fertilizer at planting, urea topdress at the big bell-mouth stage (大喇叭口). Summer rains help but my well is there — I'll irrigate at emergence if dry, and again around silking. Two or three times depending on rainfall. Corn borer is always a risk so I spray once mid-season, plus herbicide early. Two sprays total.

My husband's brother works in the city but comes back for busy seasons. I manage most of the daily work myself. I keep things the way I know them.
